strengths: Comprehensive benchmark covering 17 datasets with systematic evaluation of behavioral entanglement across primary and secondary objectives—a previously understudied phenomenon
Well-articulated modular framework clearly decomposing steering methods into direction generation, selection, and application components; facilitates standardized comparison and future research
Solid experimental execution with proper train/val/test splits, multiple models, multiple method variants, and clear presentation via Pareto curves and detailed performance heatmaps

Important empirical findings that effectiveness varies dramatically by method-model-behavior combination, and entanglement appears more pronounced in social behaviors than reasoning tasks—contrary to prior work's focus
Practical contribution: modular implementation and promised code release will enable community adoption and facilitate future steering research
weaknesses: Critical concern: 20% dynamic testing strategy not adequately justified—claimed rationale about preventing 'overfitting to spurious correlations' conflates direction generation overfitting with evaluation methodology; reduces statistical reliability and generalizability of reported metrics without clear evidence this subset produces representative results

Limited actionable insights—paper is primarily diagnostic, identifying entanglement problems without proposing novel solutions beyond using existing CAST conditional steering; lacks mechanistic understanding of why specific method-model-behavior combinations succeed or fail

Insufficient analysis of underlying causes—why does extrinsic hallucination steering fail in Qwen but succeed in Llama? Why is entanglement worse for social vs. reasoning behaviors? Without mechanistic insights, benchmark serves as lookup table rather than advancing understanding

Entanglement metric (Eq. 2) uses squared error with unclear justification; heavily weights large shifts and obscures tradeoffs between degradation on many tasks vs. catastrophic failure on single task; averaging across heterogeneous secondary tasks may hide important patterns

Severely limited model scope—only two 8B-scale instruction-tuned English models; unclear if findings generalize to larger models, different architectures, base models, or multilingual settings; raises generalization concerns for benchmarking paper

Missing critical comparisons—no comparison with other evaluation frameworks (AxBench, EasyEdit2) mentioned in related work; no comparison against training-based approaches (fine-tuning, RLHF) limits assessment of relative value

Short generation length (64 tokens) may not capture behavioral entanglement manifesting in longer-form outputs; uniform grid search acknowledged as potentially suboptimal compared to behavior-specific selection

No hyperparameter sensitivity analysis—KL divergence threshold (10%) appears arbitrary; no ablations on layer search range or coefficient range; no error bars or significance tests despite evaluating on 20% of data
Incomplete GitHub link in abstract raises reproducibility concerns; limited discussion of computational costs; no exploration of token position effects despite prior work suggesting importance

strengths: Addresses important gap in systematic evaluation of behavioral entanglement in steering methods
Comprehensive dataset collection across 17 datasets covering 3 primary and 10 secondary behaviors
Well-structured modular framework that decomposes steering into interpretable components (generation, selection, application)
Documents broader entanglement effects across behavioral categories (e.g., social behaviors like sycophancy) beyond prior work focusing on TruthfulQA
Generally competent experimental execution with stratified splits and appropriate dataset organization
weaknesses: Severely limited scope: only 2 models tested (both 8B instruction-tuned), vastly undermining generalizability claims for a benchmark paper. No small/large models, base models, or different architectures evaluated.
Dynamic 20% testing strategy contradicts benchmark purpose: throws away 80% of collected datasets without justification. Results less representative and reliable than using full test sets.
Limited novelty: all steering components (DiffInMeans, PCA, LAT, grid search, COSMIC, activation addition, CAST) are existing methods. Framework is factorization of existing approaches.
Limited insights: key findings (no universal best method, effectiveness-entanglement tradeoff) are unsurprising given model diversity. Lacks mechanistic explanations for why entanglement occurs.

Insufficient evaluation validation: heavy reliance on LLM-based evaluation (LLaMA-3.3-70B for hallucination, GPT-4o for subjective tasks) without human validation or inter-rater reliability. No statistical significance testing or confidence intervals.

Methodological concerns: ENTANGLEMENT metric (Eq. 2) uses L2 norm of squared changes without justification; uniform grid search acknowledged as suboptimal but used anyway; validation set reuse could cause overfitting; KL divergence threshold appears arbitrary.
Reproducibility gaps: incomplete GitHub link (placeholder text), missing details on random seeds, confidence intervals, CAST vector selection specifics. No computational cost analysis.
Questionable design choices: political views evaluation (left-leaning %) is arbitrary and potentially misusable; harmful generation steering could enable misuse; demographic bias coverage incomplete.
Insufficient comparison to related work: AxBench, EasyEdit2, and Im&Li (2025) appear very similar, but distinctions not clearly articulated. Why STEERINGCONTROL is distinctly better unclear.
Scope limitations under-emphasized in conclusions despite acknowledged constraints (English-only, instruction-tuned models only, 64 tokens, no chain-of-thought). These severely limit applicability.

strengths: Addresses a critical gap in steering research with a well-motivated focus on standardized evaluation and behavioral entanglement
Comprehensive benchmark spanning 17 datasets, 3 primary behaviors, 10 secondary behaviors, 5 methods, and 2 models
Elegant modular framework for decomposing steering methods into reusable components (direction generation, selection, application)
Systematic analysis of behavioral entanglement, revealing that social behaviors show more entanglement than reasoning tasks
Transparent discussion of limitations and honest acknowledgment of methodological trade-offs
Promised public release of code and datasets will benefit the community
weaknesses: Evaluation uses only 20% of each dataset citing computational cost, reducing test set sizes (~1000 samples per dataset) and potentially inflating performance variance; full evaluation is more appropriate for a benchmarking paper
Effectiveness metric (Eq. 1) is unstable—denominator (1-y) becomes very small when baseline performance is high, making small improvements appear disproportionately large
Entanglement metric (Eq. 2) squares differences without justification and aggregates across disparate behaviors, yielding unclear semantic meaning and obscuring which specific behaviors are affected
Limited model coverage: only two 7-8B parameter instruction-tuned models tested; no exploration of scale, architecture, or base model effects; generalizability questionable
Uniform grid search direction selection is acknowledged as suboptimal; behavior-specific optimization should be attempted for fair method comparison
No statistical rigor: missing confidence intervals, significance tests, variance reporting; all results are point estimates
Evaluation depends on external models (GPT-4o, LlamaGuard-4, Llama-3.3-70B) that may change, hindering reproducibility and introducing unmeasured biases
64-token generation limit acknowledged to potentially obscure model intentions; no chain-of-thought or reasoning allowed; unrealistic for some behaviors
Missing mechanistic depth: hypothesis that social behavior entanglement stems from 'shared prompt interpretation mechanisms' is stated without validation
No ablations on KL threshold, hyperparameter sensitivity, or explanation of dramatic failures (e.g., extrinsic hallucination on Qwen)
Key findings are somewhat expected: 'no universal best method,' 'effectiveness depends on model and behavior,' 'entanglement exists'—limited novelty or actionable insights
Dense heatmaps (Figures 3-8) are difficult to interpret visually despite containing details; lack clear takeaways about which methods work best for which scenarios
Insufficient comparison to related work (AxBench, EasyEdit2, Im & Li 2025); unclear what distinctly differentiates SteeringControl

strengths: Comprehensive and well-motivated benchmark spanning 9 safety perspectives across 18 datasets, addressing the important but understudied problem of entanglement in steering interventions

Rigorous experimental methodology with multiple models (Gemma-2-2B, Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen variants), five steering methods, and multiple configurations; includes statistical significance testing with FDR correction
Modular evaluation framework enabling flexible method composition and unified implementation of DIM, ACE, CAA, PCA, and LAT methods with clear ablations (Standard/NoKL/Conditional)
Strong reproducibility support with detailed hyperparameter tables, dataset construction procedures, prompt templates, and promised open-source code

Actionable findings highlighting critical safety tradeoffs: refusal steering (jailbreaking) compromises normative judgment by up to 26%, social behaviors show up to 76% degradation, hallucination steering shifts political views unpredictably

Honest treatment of limitations with clear discussion of scope constraints (English-only, short prompts, instruction-tuned models) and evaluation choices, including lower LLM judge agreement for DarkBench (κ=0.71)
weaknesses: Limited mechanistic understanding: paper is primarily descriptive rather than explanatory. Section 5's feature superposition hypothesis is explicitly unproven (authors acknowledge causally establishing this 'is beyond what activation-level measurement supports today'), leaving practitioners unable to understand why entanglement occurs or design better mitigation strategies

Incomplete steering coverage: only steers on 5/9 perspectives and omits symmetric refusal-induction (only includes jailbreaking), limiting understanding of steering toward positive safety behaviors despite authors' reasonable justification about indiscriminate refusal

Causality vs. correlation ambiguity: results show correlations between steering interventions and entanglement effects without ablations or mechanistic analysis to distinguish whether entanglement is fundamental, a hyperparameter artifact, or dataset-specific

Hyperparameter selection concerns: validation-set-based grid search with different layer preferences across methods (Table 14) lacks sensitivity analysis; unclear whether results represent genuine tradeoffs or optimization artifacts; one experiment excluded due to KL filter failure

Metric normalization choices limit interpretability: Entanglement metric (Eq. 2) uses squared absolute deviation without baseline normalization, making cross-perspective comparisons difficult; Effectiveness normalization by remaining headroom could mask important differences between high and low baseline scenarios

Evaluation quality limitations: DarkBench social behaviors results use LLM judges with substantially lower human agreement (κ=0.71 vs 0.86-0.92 on other datasets); authors acknowledge these should be 'indicative trends rather than precise measurements'; short-prompt evaluation (64 tokens) may not capture entanglement in longer generation contexts

Limited actionability: findings document important tradeoffs but offer minimal guidance for practitioners (which method to use? how to design steering to minimize entanglement?) and conditional steering results are mixed without clear recommendations

Striking but unexplained findings: hallucination steering shifts political views in opposite directions across models (Gemma-2-2B leftward, Llama-3.1-8B rightward), suggesting model-specific confounds that deserve mechanistic investigation

strengths: Comprehensive and systematic evaluation across multiple steering methods, models, and safety perspectives with sound experimental methodology (FDR-corrected statistical tests, validation of LLM judges against human annotation κ=0.86-0.92)

Useful modular benchmark infrastructure implementing five steering methods with interchangeable components enabling fair comparison and reproducibility efforts (detailed hyperparameters, computational costs, promised code release)
Addresses important problem: unintended side effects of safety interventions are critical for practitioners and underexplored at scale across multiple safety dimensions
Well-documented benchmark aggregating 18 datasets across 9 safety perspectives with proper data stratification, splits, and clear presentation of complex results
weaknesses: Limited novelty: benchmark primarily aggregates existing datasets and implements existing steering methods (DIM, ACE, CAA, PCA, LAT); concept of objective entanglement is known in ML; contribution is mainly systematic measurement, not fundamental new insights or methods

Main findings are descriptive but somewhat expected: that steering one behavior affects others is unsurprising without deep mechanistic understanding of why or actionable solutions beyond partial mitigation via conditional steering

Severely limited scope reduces generalizability: only 2B-8B instruction-tuned models (unclear if findings hold for 70B+ frontier models with different architectures), only English datasets, only inference-time static vectors, no comparison with training-based steering baselines

Mechanistic understanding lacking and speculative: Section 5's feature superposition hypothesis is plausible but explicitly untested; paper identifies entanglement patterns but not causal mechanisms, preventing principled solution design

Methodological concerns: (1) Effectiveness normalization by (1-y_d) makes cross-perspective comparison problematic; (2) deliberate choice not to normalize entanglement creates interpretability issues; (3) KL divergence threshold (0.1) is arbitrary with no ablation; (4) grid search on validation set risks overfitting

Experimental design imbalance: only 3 perspectives steered but 9 evaluated—why these three? Why not steer social behaviors or normative judgment? Limits understanding of causal steering-entanglement relationships

Presentation overwhelmed by results: Figures 7-15 contain hundreds of numbers in dense heat-map format, four 'Key Finding' boxes dilute main message, entanglement decomposition (valuable Table 16) relegated to appendix, difficult to extract actionable insights

Limited practical guidance: paper shows that entanglement occurs but provides minimal solutions; conditional steering (CAST) only partially mitigates effects and fails on bias tasks; no design principles or concrete recommendations for practitioners or method developers

strengths: Comprehensive evaluation across 9 safety perspectives and 18 datasets with rigorous methodology (FDR-corrected statistics, human-LLM agreement validation)
Addresses critical gap by systematically measuring 'entanglement'—cross-safety interference—which is underexplored in steering literature
Well-designed modular framework enabling fair comparison of 5 steering methods with interchangeable components (direction generation/selection/application)

Actionable empirical findings: social behaviors vulnerable to 76% degradation, refusal steering compromises normative judgment (≤26%), hallucination steering produces opposite political shifts across models
Excellent reproducibility: extensive hyperparameter tables, transparent methodology, human agreement statistics (κ=0.860-0.920), promised code release, honest limitations discussion
Novel analysis decomposing entanglement into harmful vs. beneficial components (84.3% harmful); findings are model-specific suggesting non-universal patterns
Multiple evaluation settings (Standard/NoKL/Conditional) and scale consistency checks across model sizes demonstrate thoroughness
weaknesses: Limited explanatory power: primarily descriptive (what happens) rather than mechanistic (why); proposed feature superposition hypothesis acknowledged as unvalidated and separate from empirical claims

Narrow steering scope: only 5 perspectives steered toward, cannot determine if entanglement is universal or specific to these objectives; refusal-induction excluded (reasonable but limits completeness)

Evaluation constraints: DarkBench uses lower human-LLM agreement (κ=0.71) yet features prominently; token position fixed to post-instruction despite prior work suggesting better alternatives; only 64 tokens generated limiting assessment of longer-form reasoning
Limited model diversity: restricted to relatively small models (2B-8B); no large frontier models (GPT-3.5, Claude, larger open models); unclear if patterns generalize
Lack of prescriptive guidance: identifies problems but offers no solutions; conditional steering improvements ad-hoc; no principled framework for optimizing effectiveness-entanglement tradeoff

Incomplete analysis of context-dependence: why do methods produce opposite effects across models (e.g., political views)? Why within-bias tradeoffs? These mysteries hint at important structure but remain uninvestigated

Presentation issues: Figure 3 overlapping bars hard to read; claims like 'up to 76% degradation' lack clarity (max? mean?); asymmetric normalization of effectiveness vs. entanglement (Eq. 1 vs. 2) justified but inelegant
